mainTopic: Words written but not read, אגדות about משה's wealth and the gift of the תורה, the qualities of a נביא, and the משנה on feeding the family and animals of someone forbidden by נדר.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a list of words that are written in תנ״ך but not read aloud. רב אחא בר אדא then reports that in ארץ ישראל one long פסוק was split into three. The topic turns to אגדה about משה. From ״פסל לך״ we learn that משה grew rich from the leftover chips of the לוחות. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא adds that the תורה was first given only to משה, who generously shared it. After several challenges, the גמרא narrows this to say that only the deep analysis (פילפולא) was his alone. רבי יוחנן teaches that the שכינה rests only on someone mighty, wealthy, wise, and humble, and proves each quality from משה. He also teaches that all the נביאים were wealthy, which the גמרא shows from משה, שמואל, עמוס, and יונה, along with רבא's comment that שמואל was even more careful than משה. Finally the משנה returns to the laws of נדרים: one may feed the wife and children of a man forbidden to benefit from him, but not his animals. רבי אליעזר distinguishes kosher from non-kosher animals, and his explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the list of words written but not read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its list of words that are written in the text but are not said aloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word "this" in "the מצוה," the word "bend" in "the archer," the word "five" in "the south side," and the word "if" in "that a near kinsman": these are written but not read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started earlier. The list is of words that appear in the written פסוק but are skipped when the פסוק is read aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item names one word and identifies the פסוק it comes from by a nearby word. The closing line, הלין כתבן ולא קריין, labels the whole group. These are the opposite of the earlier list of words that are read but not written (קריין ולא כתבן).

keyTerms.meaning: Written but not read: a word that appears in the text but is not said aloud
A redeemer or near relative (from רות)

steps.whatToRemember: The text of תנ״ך has a few words that are written but not read, and a few that are read but not written. Both are part of the מסורה, the received tradition about the text.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a disagreement or a mistake in the text. It is an accepted tradition that the written form and the spoken reading differ in these places.

phrases.english: "This" of "the מצוה,"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:1. Each item gives a word, then a nearby word so you can tell which פסוק it comes from.

phrases.english: "Bend" of "the archer,"
"Five" of "the south side,"
"If" of "that a near kinsman":
these are written but not read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from the previous עמוד of words that are written but not read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These four words are written in the text but are not read aloud.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל one verse was split into three
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אדא reports that in ארץ ישראל they divided שמות 19:9 into three separate פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אדא said: In the West they divide this verse into three verses: "And ה׳ said to משה: Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud..."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר אדא adds another fact about how the text is handled. In ארץ ישראל, one פסוק that is a single long verse elsewhere was broken into three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of traditions about the form of the text, here about where a פסוק begins and ends. Only the opening words of the פסוק are quoted, but the whole פסוק is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל (seen from בבל)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Adda said:
In the West they divide this verse
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: into three verses:
"And the Lord said to Moses,
phrases.notes: שמות 19:9. Only the start is quoted, but he means the whole long פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָּא אֵלֶיךָ בְּעַב הֶעָנָן״.
phrases.english: behold, I come to you in a thick cloud."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא פָּסְקִין לְהָדֵין פְּסוּקָא לִתְלָתָא פְּסוּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another tradition about the form of the text, this time about verse division.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, שמות 19:9 was divided into three פסוקים.

steps.title: משה became wealthy from the chips of the לוחות
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא reads ״פסל לך״ as "the chips are yours" and teaches that משה's wealth came from the leftovers of carving the second לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: משה became wealthy only from the leftover chips of the לוחות, as it says, "Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones." This means: their chips will be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, an אגדה about משה. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains where משה's wealth came from, using a פסוק about the second לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פסל, "carve," sounds like פסולת, the leftover chips from carving. The extra word לך, "for you," is read as "the chips belong to you." So the valuable stone chips from carving the לוחות became משה's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Waste, the chips left over from carving
The stone tablets of the Covenant

steps.whyThisMatters: This same reading of ״פסל לך״ becomes the basis for the next teaching about who the תורה was given to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
Moses did not become wealthy
except from the waste of the tablets,
as it is stated: "Carve for yourself
phrases.notes: שמות 34:1. פסל, "carve," sounds like פסולת, the leftover chips.

phrases.english: two tablets of stone like the first ones":
their waste shall be yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הֶעֱשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה אֶלָּא מִפְּסוֹלְתָּן שֶׁל לוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, an אגדה about משה, unrelated to the list of textual traditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's wealth came from the leftover chips of the second לוחות, learned from ״פסל לך״.

steps.title: The תורה was given to משה, and he shared it generously
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא compares ״כתב לך״ to ״פסל לך״: just as the chips belonged to משה, so did the writing. But משה generously gave the תורה to ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The תורה was given only to משה and his descendants, as it says "Write for yourself" and "Carve for yourself." Just as the chips are yours, so too the writing is yours. משה acted generously with it and gave it to ישראל. About him the פסוק says: "One with a good eye will be blessed."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא builds on the previous teaching. He uses the matching word לך in two פסוקים to say the תורה itself first belonged to משה, and then praises משה for sharing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ״כתב לך״ and ״פסל לך״ use the word לך, "for you." Since we already know the chips were משה's own, the matching wording teaches that the writing, meaning the תורה, was his too. משה chose to give it to all of ישראל, and the פסוק in משלי about a generous person is applied to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too: a comparison formula

steps.whatToRemember: ״פסל לך״ teaches that the chips of the לוחות were משה's, and ״כתב לך״ teaches the same about the תורה. משה's generosity is the reason all of ישראל received the תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
The Torah was not given
except to Moses and his descendants,
as it is stated: "Write for yourself," "Carve for yourself":
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27 and שמות 34:1. The shared word לך links the two.

phrases.english: just as their waste is yours,
so too their writing is yours.
Moses treated it with a good eye
phrases.notes: A "good eye" means being generous rather than stingy.

phrases.english: and gave it to Israel,
and about him the verse says:
"He that has a good eye shall be blessed, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה פְּסוֹלְתָּן שֶׁלְּךָ — אַף כְּתָבָן שֶׁלְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the previous step's reading of ״פסל לך״ and extends it to ״כתב לך״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה was first given only to משה and his descendants, and משה generously gave it to ישראל.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges from a פסוק saying משה was commanded to teach
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes דברים 4:14, where משה says ה׳ commanded him to teach the people. That seems to show the תורה was meant for ישראל from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: "And ה׳ commanded me at that time to teach you."
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the previous claim that the תורה belonged only to משה. He brings a פסוק saying משה was ordered to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said משה generously chose to give the תורה away. If ה׳ commanded משה to teach, then teaching was an obligation, not a gift.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection:
"And ה׳ commanded me at that time
to teach you"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement in Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תורה belonged only to משה and he chose to share it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says ה׳ commanded משה to teach, so teaching was required and not a free gift

steps.title: The פסוק is split: ה׳ commanded me, and I chose to teach you
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the פסוק in two parts. ה׳ gave the commands to משה, and משה on his own passed them to the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: He commanded me, and I passed it on to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 4 by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Commanded me" refers only to ה׳ giving משה the תורה. "To teach you" describes what משה decided to do himself, so the generous gift still stands.

phrases.english: And He commanded me,
and I [passed it on] to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק by splitting it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means ה׳ ordered משה to teach
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ commanded משה, and משה chose to teach

steps.title: A second פסוק: I taught you as ה׳ commanded me
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק, דברים 4:5, seems to say that משה's teaching was itself what ה׳ commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: "See, I have taught you statutes and laws, as ה׳ my God commanded me."
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues with a second פסוק that ties משה's teaching directly to ה׳'s command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words "as ה׳ commanded me" seem to describe the teaching itself. That makes the teaching sound required.

phrases.english: "See, I have taught you statutes and laws
as ה׳ my God commanded me"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for the same challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה's teaching is described as following ה׳'s command

steps.title: Same answer: ה׳ commanded me, and I taught you
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same split reading as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Me He commanded, and I taught you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second פסוק the same way it answered the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command went to משה. The teaching was משה's own generous step.

phrases.english: Me He commanded, and I [taught] you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the receiving was commanded, and the teaching was voluntary

steps.title: A third פסוק: write this song and teach it
steps.stepSummary: דברים 31:19 tells them to write the song and teach it to ישראל, which looks like a direct order to share the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And now write for yourselves this song."
steps.whatsHappening: A third proof is brought. This פסוק seems to command teaching outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split reading is harder to use here, because the פסוק itself orders writing and teaching the people.

phrases.english: "And now write for yourselves
this song"
phrases.notes: דברים 31:19. The פסוק goes on: "and teach it to בני ישראל."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַתָּה כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third proof for the same challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly commands writing and teaching

steps.title: Only the song had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the command covers only the song of הַאֲזִינוּ, not the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The song alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the command to just the song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the song had to be taught, the rest of the תורה could still be משה's own gift.

phrases.english: The song alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the command
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The command covers the whole תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: The command covers only the song

steps.title: The song is a witness, so the whole תורה must be included
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק continues that the song will be a witness among ישראל. That only works if they have the מצוות the song warns about.
steps.simpleTranslation: "So that this song will be for Me as a witness among בני ישראל"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer by reading further in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness against ישראל only makes sense if they were given the whole תורה to keep. So the command to teach must reach beyond the song.

phrases.english: "So that this song will be for Me
as a witness among the children of Israel"!
phrases.notes: Same פסוק. The song can only testify about מצוות the people were actually given.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה לִּי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לְעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that only the song had to be taught
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness requires that the whole תורה was given to the people

steps.title: Only the deep analysis was given to משה alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the whole תורה was given to ישראל, and only its sharp, deep analysis was given to משה alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was just the deep analysis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on saying the whole תורה was משה's alone. It narrows Step 4 to the deep reasoning of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself was given to everyone. What belonged to משה, and what he generously shared, was the פילפולא, the deep sharp understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: sharp, deep analysis of the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's idea is limited: the תורה was given to all of ישראל, and only the deep analysis was משה's to give.

phrases.english: Rather, [it was] just the sharp analysis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 11 by narrowing Step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole תורה was given only to משה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the deep analysis was given to משה alone

steps.title: The שכינה rests only on someone mighty, wealthy, wise, and humble
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists four qualities needed for the שכינה to rest on a person, and says all four are learned from משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: הקדוש ברוך הוא rests His שכינה only on someone mighty, wealthy, wise, and humble, and we learn all of them from משה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens about the qualities of a prophet. The גמרא will now prove each quality from משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a list to prove. Each of the four qualities will need a source showing משה had it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not rest His Divine Presence

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר וְחָכָם וְעָנָיו,
phrases.english: except on one who is mighty, wealthy, wise, and humble,
and all of them [we learn] from Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic connected to משה, whose wealth was discussed in Step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה rests only on someone mighty, wealthy, wise, and humble, and משה is the model for all four

steps.title: First proof of strength: משה spread the tent over the tall boards
steps.stepSummary: משה spread the tent over the משכן by himself, and the boards were ten אמות tall. So he must have been strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mighty: as it says, "And he spread the tent over the משכן," and the master said that משה our teacher spread it himself. And it says, "Ten אמות is the length of a board."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving the first quality, strength, from the building of the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facts are combined: משה put up the covering alone, and the boards were ten אמות high. Lifting a covering that high by yourself seems to need great strength.

phrases.english: Mighty, as it is written:
"And he spread the tent over the Mishkan,"
and the master said: Moshe our teacher spread it,
and it is written: "Ten cubits is the length of a board, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּבּוֹר, דִּכְתִיב: וַיִּפְרֹשׂ אֶת הָאֹהֶל עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first quality listed in Step 13

steps.title: Maybe he was just tall and thin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: being able to reach high only shows that משה was tall, not that he was strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he was tall and thin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaching over ten-אמה boards proves height, not strength. A tall, thin man could do it too.

phrases.english: Say that he was tall and thin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the claim that משה was mighty still stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof shows height, not strength

steps.title: Better proof: משה lifted and threw the heavy stone לוחות
steps.stepSummary: משה held and threw the two לוחות, and a ברייתא says each was six by six by three טפחים of stone. Lifting that shows real strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from this פסוק: "And I grabbed the two tablets and threw them from my two hands and broke them." And a ברייתא teaches: the לוחות were six long, six wide, and three thick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected proof with a stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוחות were huge blocks of stone. Lifting them and throwing them proves strength, which height alone cannot explain.

keyTerms.meaning: the tablets of the עשרת הדברות

phrases.english: Rather, from this verse, as it is written:
"And I grabbed hold of the two tablets
and threw them from my two hands and broke them,"
and it was taught [in a ברייתא]:

phrases.aramaic: הַלּוּחוֹת אׇרְכָּן שִׁשָּׁה וְרׇחְבָּן שִׁשָּׁה וְעׇבְיָין שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: The tablets: their length was six, their width six, and their thickness three.
phrases.notes: These are measured in טפחים, handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in Step 15
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 9:17 together with the ברייתא about the size of the לוחות

steps.title: משה was wealthy: the leftover stone of the לוחות was his
steps.stepSummary: The words 'carve for yourself' teach that the leftover chips of the לוחות belonged to משה, which made him rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wealthy: 'Carve for yourself' teaches that the leftover chips will be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: Having proven that משה was strong, the גמרא now proves the next quality on the list: that he was wealthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'for yourself' (לָךְ) is read as 'the scraps are for you.' Since the לוחות were made of precious stone, the leftover chips made משה rich.

phrases.english: Wealthy — 'Carve for yourself,'
phrases.notes: שמות 34:1, where ה׳ tells משה to carve the second לוחות.

phrases.english: their leftover scraps shall be yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from strength to the second quality in רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 34:1, 'פסל לך', read as 'the scraps are yours'

steps.title: משה was wise: he received 49 of the 50 gates of understanding
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל teach that 50 gates of understanding exist, and משה got all of them but one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wise: from what רב and שמואל both say. Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to משה except one, as it says 'You made him a little less than God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third quality, that משה was wise, using a teaching of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Understanding is pictured as 50 'gates' or levels. משה reached 49 of them. The פסוק 'You made him a little less than God' shows he was missing only one, the very highest level.

phrases.english: Wise — from רב and שמואל, who both say:
Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world,
and all of them were given to משה except one,
as it says: 'You made him a little less than God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the list of four qualities.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב and שמואל's teaching of the 50 gates, backed by תהלים 8:6

steps.title: משה was humble: the תורה says so outright
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק states openly that משה was very humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: Humble: as it is written, 'And the man משה was very humble.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last of the four qualities, humility, with a פסוק that says it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no extra reasoning is needed, because the פסוק plainly states it. This finishes the proof that משה had all four qualities needed for the שכינה to rest on a person.
steps.whatToRemember: All four qualities (strong, wealthy, wise, humble) are now proven from משה.

phrases.english: Humble — as it is written:
'And the man משה was very humble.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the list; closes the discussion of the four qualities.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: all the prophets were wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says every נביא was wealthy, and names four examples it is learned from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All the prophets were wealthy. How do we know? From משה, שמואל, עמוס and יונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching of רבי יוחנן is introduced. It sets up the proofs that follow, one for each prophet he names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on wealth being one of the qualities of a prophet. רבי יוחנן gives four test cases, and the גמרא will now go through them one by one to show each was rich.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
All the prophets were wealthy.
From where do we know? From משה, from שמואל, from עמוס and from יונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַנְּבִיאִים עֲשִׁירִים הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the wealth theme from משה alone to all the prophets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every prophet was wealthy, as seen from משה, שמואל, עמוס and יונה.

steps.title: First try for משה: 'I did not take a single donkey'
steps.stepSummary: משה said he never took anyone's donkey. Since taking one for free would be plain theft, he must mean he never even paid for one, so he must have been rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה: as it is written, 'I did not take a single donkey from them.' If it means without paying, is he just saying he isn't a thief? Rather, it means he didn't take one even for pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that משה was wealthy from his words 'I did not take one donkey from them.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I never stole a donkey' would be nothing to boast about. So the גמרא reads it as 'I never even rented or bought one from them.' Not needing anything from others suggests he was rich.

phrases.english: משה — as it is written:
'I did not take a single donkey from them.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:15, said by משה about קרח and his group.

phrases.english: If it means without payment,
is he only setting himself apart from someone who takes without paying?
Rather, it means not even for payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה — דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא חֲמוֹר אֶחָד מֵהֶם נָשָׂאתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First proof for the first name on רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 16:15, read as 'not even for pay'

steps.title: Rejected: maybe משה was poor
steps.stepSummary: Not paying for a donkey could just mean he could not afford one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it was because he was poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Never buying or renting a donkey fits a poor man just as well as a rich man. So the פסוק proves nothing about wealth.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up עָנִי (poor) here with עָנָיו (humble) from step 19. They look alike but mean different things.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was because he was poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 21's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The donkey proof for משה's wealth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same behavior fits a poor man, so it does not show wealth.

steps.title: Better proof for משה: the leftover stone of the לוחות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to 'carve for yourself': the scraps of the לוחות were his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is learned from 'Carve for yourself': their scraps shall be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the donkey proof, the גמרא uses the earlier proof from the leftover stone of the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same source used in step 17. It works here because it shows wealth actually being given to משה, unlike the donkey פסוק, which could fit a poor man too.

phrases.english: Rather, from 'Carve for yourself' —
their scraps shall be yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with the source from step 17.

steps.title: First try for שמואל: 'Whose ox or donkey have I taken?'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל said he never took anyone's ox or donkey. Taking for free would be theft, so he must mean even for pay, which would show he was rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל: as it is written, 'Here I am, testify against me before ה׳ and His anointed: whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken?' If for free, is he just saying he isn't a thief? Rather, even for pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same kind of proof for שמואל, using his own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic matches step 21 exactly. Not stealing is nothing to boast about, so he must mean he never even paid to use someone's animals, which suggests wealth.

phrases.english: שמואל — as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִנְנִי עֲנוּ בִי נֶגֶד ה׳ וְנֶגֶד מְשִׁיחוֹ
phrases.english: 'Here I am, testify against me before ה׳ and before His anointed:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שׁוֹר מִי לָקַחְתִּי וַחֲמוֹר מִי לָקַחְתִּי״.
phrases.english: whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken?'
If it means for free,
is he only setting himself apart from someone who takes for free?!
Rather, it means not even for pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל, דִּכְתִיב: ״הִנְנִי עֲנוּ בִי נֶגֶד ה׳ וְנֶגֶד מְשִׁיחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second name on רבי יוחנן's list, using the same pattern as step 21.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 12:3, read as 'not even for pay'

steps.title: Rejected: maybe שמואל was poor
steps.stepSummary: Same rejection as for משה: perhaps he simply could not afford to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he was poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for שמואל the same way it rejected the one for משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not paying for animals fits poverty as well as wealth, so the פסוק does not prove שמואל was rich.

phrases.english: Perhaps he was poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 24's proof, just like step 22 did for משה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ox and donkey proof for שמואל's wealth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same behavior fits a poor man.

steps.title: Better proof for שמואל: his house went with him wherever he traveled
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'his return was to רמה, for his house was there,' and רבא explains that his household traveled with him everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from here: 'And his return was to רמה, for there was his house.' And רבא said: everywhere he went, his house was with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for שמואל's wealth from a different פסוק, explained by רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'there was his house' as saying that wherever שמואל went, he brought his household with him. Moving a whole household around takes money, so this shows he was wealthy.
steps.whatToRemember: Pattern for both משה and שמואל: a 'didn't take a donkey' proof is rejected (maybe he was poor) and replaced by a source that shows actual wealth.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'And his return was to רמה, for there was his house,'
and רבא said:
everywhere he went, his house was with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָכָא: ״וּתְשֻׁבָתוֹ הָרָמָתָה כִּי שָׁם בֵּיתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a stronger one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 7:17 as explained by רבא

steps.title: שמואל was even more careful than משה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the praise of שמואל is greater than the praise of משה. משה never took a donkey against the owner's will, even for pay. שמואל never rented anything, even when the owner was happy to let him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is said about שמואל is greater than what is said about משה. About משה it says 'I have not taken one donkey from them,' meaning even for pay. About שמואל, he would not rent something even when the owner agreed, as it says 'You have not cheated us and you have not oppressed us.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last two steps compared משה and שמואל, רבא adds a side comment: שמואל's honesty went even further than משה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's פסוק means he never forced anyone to give him an animal, even if he would have paid. שמואל's פסוק uses the word רַצּוֹתָנוּ, which sounds like רָצוֹן (consent). So he did not even rent things from people who were willing. This is a side point and does not continue the proof about wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: You have not oppressed us (read here as linked to רָצוֹן)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Greater is what is said about Shmuel
than what is said about Moshe,
for about Moshe our teacher it is written:
"Not one donkey of theirs have I taken,"
meaning not even for pay,
phrases.notes: He means משה never took one against the owner's will, even if he would have paid for it.

phrases.english: whereas about Shmuel,
even with the owner's consent he did not rent it,
as it is written:
"And they said: You have not cheated us
and you have not oppressed us, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 12:4. רַצּוֹתָנוּ sounds like רָצוֹן, willingness, so he didn't even rent things from willing owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּשְׁמוּאֵל יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment that grows out of comparing the פסוקים about משה and שמואל in the steps before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל refused even consensual rentals, which goes beyond משה's refusal to take things against an owner's will.

steps.title: עמוס was wealthy
steps.stepSummary: עמוס said he was a herdsman and tended sycamores. רב יוסף's translation shows that he owned flocks and sycamore fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: עמוס was wealthy, as it is written: 'עמוס answered אמציה: I am not a נביא or a נביא's son; I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamores.' As רב יוסף translates: 'For I own flocks, and I have sycamores in the lowland.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main line and proves that the נביא עמוס was wealthy too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read on its own, 'herdsman' might sound like a poor worker. רב יוסף's Aramaic translation turns it into 'owner of flocks' and adds that he owned sycamore fields. So עמוס was a man of property, which fits the rule that נביאים are wealthy.

phrases.english: Amos was wealthy, as it is written:
"And Amos answered and said to Amatzyah:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָבִיא אָנֹכִי וְלֹא בֶן נָבִיא אָנֹכִי
phrases.english: I am not a prophet, nor am I a prophet's son,
but I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamores,"
as Rav Yosef translates it:
"For I am an owner of flocks
and I have sycamores in the lowland, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבא's side comment to the list of wealthy נביאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 7:14 as translated by רב יוסף

steps.title: יונה was wealthy
steps.stepSummary: יונה 'paid its fare,' and רבי יוחנן reads this to mean he paid for the whole ship. רבי רומנוס adds that this cost four thousand gold dinars.
steps.simpleTranslation: יונה was wealthy, as it is written: 'He paid its fare and went down into it.' רבי יוחנן said: He paid the fare of the whole ship. רבי רומנוס said: The fare of the ship was four thousand gold דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that יונה was wealthy from the way he paid to board the ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'its fare,' meaning the ship's fare and not just his own ticket. So רבי יוחנן says he hired the entire ship. רבי רומנוס gives the price, four thousand gold dinars, which shows how rich יונה was.

phrases.english: Jonah was wealthy, as it is written:
"And he paid its fare and went down into it,"
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
he paid the fare of the entire ship.
Rabbi Romanus said:
The fare of the ship
was four thousand gold dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next proof in the same list of wealthy נביאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יונה 1:3 as explained by רבי יוחנן and רבי רומנוס
steps.whatToRemember: Every נביא is shown to be wealthy: משה from the scraps of the לוחות, שמואל from his traveling household, עמוס from his flocks and fields, and יונה from hiring a whole ship.

steps.title: משה kept forgetting the תורה until it was given as a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that at first משה would learn תורה and forget it. Only once ה׳ gave it to him as a gift did he keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: At first משה would learn תורה and forget it, until it was given to him as a gift, as it says: 'And He gave to משה, when He finished speaking with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי יוחנן about משה: he could not hold on to the תורה he learned until ה׳ gave it to him as a present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the word 'וַיִּתֵּן', 'and He gave', which shows the תורה was a gift. Learning on his own was not enough for משה to remember. Once the תורה became his as a gift, it stayed with him.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
At first Moshe would
learn Torah and forget it,
until it was given to him as a gift,
as it is said:
"And He gave to Moshe
when He finished speaking with him."
phrases.notes: שמות 31:18. The word "gave" is what shows it was a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּתְּחִלָּה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה לָמֵד תּוֹרָה וּמְשַׁכְּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of wealthy נביאים ends, the גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יוחנן about משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה could not hold on to the תורה through his own learning until ה׳ gave it to him as a gift.

steps.title: He may feed the man's wife and children
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may still feed the wife and children of a man who is forbidden by נדר to benefit from him, even though that man is obligated to support them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He may feed the man's wife and his children, even though the man is obligated to provide their food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has finished its long side story and now brings the next ruling of the משנה. It says you may feed the wife and children of someone who is forbidden by נדר to benefit from you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think this is not allowed, since the husband would otherwise have to buy their food, so he saves money. The משנה still permits it. The food goes straight to the wife and children, and the husband only gains indirectly.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' who feeds is the person whose things are forbidden to the other man. The 'his wife and children' belong to the man who is forbidden to benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast with animals in the next line. Feeding people is allowed, but feeding a man's animals raises a different question.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ וְזָן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו
phrases.english: MISHNA: And he may feed his wife and his children
phrases.notes: "He" is the man whose things the other man may not benefit from. The wife and children belong to that other man.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב בִּמְזוֹנוֹתָן
phrases.english: even though he is obligated in their food

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְזָן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה about נביאים to the halachic text of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeding the wife and children of someone forbidden to benefit from you is allowed, even though he is obligated to support them.

steps.title: He may not feed the man's animals
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that he may not feed the man's animal, whether it is non-kosher or kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he may not feed the man's animal, whether it is non-kosher or kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns from the family to the animals. The first opinion forbids feeding the man's animal of any kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal is the owner's property. Feeding it directly helps the owner, because his animal stays healthy and keeps its value. So this counts as forbidden benefit, unlike feeding his wife and children.

phrases.english: But he may not feed his animal
whether non-kosher or kosher

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 31: people may be fed, but animals may not
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man's animals may not be fed, whether kosher or non-kosher.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר splits kosher from non-kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees. He may feed a non-kosher animal but not a kosher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He may feed the non-kosher animal, but he may not feed the kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees with the first one. רבי אליעזר permits feeding a non-kosher animal and forbids feeding a kosher one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treated all animals the same. רבי אליעזר draws a line between them, which suggests the owner does not benefit in the same way from each kind. He does not give his reason yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says
He may feed the non-kosher one
and he may not feed the kosher one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion to the תנא קמא in step 32
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeding a non-kosher animal is allowed. Feeding a kosher animal is forbidden.

steps.title: The חכמים ask what the difference is
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי אליעזר why a kosher animal should be treated differently from a non-kosher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What is the difference between a non-kosher and a kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The other חכמים challenge רבי אליעזר to explain his distinction. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of animal belong to the owner, and he gains when either is fed. So the חכמים want to know why one kind should be permitted and the other forbidden.

phrases.english: They said to him
What is the difference between non-kosher and kosher?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ מָה בֵּין טְמֵאָה לִטְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's distinction in step 33
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a kosher animal is different from a non-kosher one for this נדר

steps.title: רבי אליעזר begins his answer: a kosher animal's body belongs to its owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that a kosher animal's soul belongs to Heaven but its body belongs to the owner. He then starts to describe the non-kosher animal, and that explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Because a kosher animal's soul belongs to Heaven and its body belongs to him. And a non-kosher animal...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר starts to explain his view. A kosher animal's body is fully the owner's, so feeding it helps him directly. His explanation of the non-kosher animal continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner can slaughter and eat a kosher animal, so its body is entirely his to use. Fattening it up therefore benefits him directly. He has not yet explained how a non-kosher animal is different; that comes next.

phrases.english: He said to them
That the kosher one, its soul is to Heaven
and its body is his
And a non-kosher one

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ שֶׁהַטְּהוֹרָה נַפְשָׁהּ לַשָּׁמַיִם וְגוּפָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A kosher animal's body belongs to the owner, since he can eat it, so feeding it benefits him directly. The contrast with a non-kosher animal is still being explained.
